sources.title: Report on Cultural Mapping of India under UNESCO's Programme on Cultural Industries and Copyright Policies and Partnerships
sources.author: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
sources.publisher: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
sources.source_family: IGNCA cultural-mapping report; alternate IGNCA paths are the same report
sources.locator: Printed p94, Dhumpa table: Provenance, Description and Information Source fields; cover p1 identifies title/contract.
sources.inspection: Complete original-domain search-indexed p94 entry and cover text inspected. Direct PDF requests timed out; original visual check requested from coordinator. No local capture made by Anvesha.
supports: Entry locates the described practice in Khandapada, Nayagarh.
Describes a hollow cylinder six to seven feet long made from bark of Bhendiamardan or Mayi tree, extracted during the rainy season.
Describes a principal singer, four or five chorus singers, six or eight Kathias or stick drummers, a pot-bellied performer and a Gotipua dancer.
Describes singing with accompanying instruments and Kathias striking the cylinder.
The entry cites personal interaction with BibutiBhusan Mardaraja, identified as the Raja of Khandapara.
sources.recommended_use: A concise explicitly attributed Khandapada ensemble description; distinguish the instrument from the combined practice of singing and playing. Exact headcounts optional and local only.
limits: A local attributed descriptive account, not a survey of all Dhumpa instruments or performers.
Do not substitute bamboo for the entry's bark material, or infer two established regional types from disagreement alone.
The suspended-cylinder/belly-motion sentence is grammatically unclear; omit detailed mechanics, precise direction or sonic-causation explanation.
Omit origin, patron chronology, BBC-film and 'dying' status claims; not independently verified and unnecessary.
The presence of UNESCO in the report title does not mean UNESCO heritage inscription.
No botanical species identity inferred from local tree names.
Cover does not expose publication date. IGNCA annual-report support separately records project submission March2006, not necessarily public release date.

sources.title: Dhumpa Sangeet enthrals audience
sources.author: Post News Network
sources.source_family: OrissaPOST news report; AMP duplicate is not independent evidence
sources.locator: Headline/byline/date and first two narrative paragraphs; final Dhumpa paragraph inspected but unsupported origin assertion excluded.
sources.inspection: Original article directly opened and complete short narrative read.
supports: Report dated17September2018 describes a Bhubaneswar cultural programme at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, in collaboration with Infosys Foundation.
Opening Dhumpa song is attributed to the group named Gangadhar Dhumpa Sangeet Parishad in the report.
The report links Khandapada songs with rainy-season singing and Radha-Krishna love themes.
sources.recommended_use: A named, dated reported performance that brings the ensemble discussion into a public programme; limited attributed repertoire context optional.
limits: Use the report's exact group name Gangadhar; do not silently correct to Gadadhar or equate groups without evidence.
Reporter spelling Bharitya Vidya Bhawan may be normalized to conventional institution name, without changing identity.
Do not present reporter assessment 'sweet and melodious' as personal listening.
Programme branding 'Near Extinct Folk Art' is not a measured present-day population finding.
No attendance, full repertoire, artist incomes or durable revival result established.

sources.locator: Programme performance entry18: Alok Bishoyi – Dhumpa Vadya. Cover identifies festival21–25June2022 in New Delhi. Specific performance day/page pending visual column check.

supports: The official21–25June2022Jyotirgamaya programme lists Alok Bishoyi with Dhumpa Vadya.
Programme places Dhumpa within a festival focused on performers and musical instruments.
sources.recommended_use: Describe as a programme listing or scheduled appearance, not independently witnessed completed performance.
limits: Do not infer programme listing proves actual performance, attendance, training outcomes or revival.
Exact individual day/time/page requires visual confirmation; extracted columns are interleaved.
Brochure event2022 must not be dated2026or2025from search-engine crawl/upload estimates.
Do not infer instrument making by Bishoyi merely because other brochure sessions include workshops.

material_conflict.finding: IGNCA's named local account specifies tree bark. Generic online descriptions call the instrument bamboo, sometimes reproducing Wikipedia wording.
material_conflict.handling: Use the well-located Khandapada description with attribution; do not label all Dhumpa bamboo, invent a regional taxonomy, or write a lengthy conflict lecture.

Wikipedia, copied descriptions in tourism/blog/video pages and GK pages are not independent construction evidence.
